rules.name: wait-without-limit
rules.message: A wait loop with no limit runs forever when what it waits for never comes: one was left running in the background for hours on 2026-10-16. Give it a limit (`SECONDS=0; until …; do sleep 2; [ $SECONDS -gt 90 ] && break; done`, or `timeout 90 …`).
blocks: D=$(ls -d picks/s1); until [ -f $D/a.done.json ] && [ -f $D/b.done.json ]; do sleep 2; done; cat $D/a.done.json
until curl -s localhost:3000; do sleep 1; done
allows: SECONDS=0; until [ -f x ]; do sleep 2; [ $SECONDS -gt 90 ] && break; done
timeout 60 bash -c 'until [ -f x ]; do sleep 1; done'
for i in 1 2 3; do echo $i; done

rules.name: force-push-to-main
rules.message: A forced push to main rewrites shared history. Push to a branch and open a pull request.

rules.name: verdict-through-tail
rules.message: Piping a test through tail/head/grep (or Select-Object, Select-String) hides its verdict: the exit code becomes the pipe's (lesson 44, P-1). Start the command with `set -o pipefail &&`, or save the output to a file and read it.
blocks: npm test --silent 2>&1 | tail -4 && git commit -m x
allows: node scripts/lessons.mjs --check > out.txt 2>&1; cat out.txt; git diff lessons/en | head -30

rules.name: script-cut-by-select-first
rules.message: `| Select-Object -First` stops the command as soon as it has its lines: a script is cut off before it finishes or cleans up, and its exit code is lost (P-1). Save the output to a file and read the lines you want.
allows: node x.mjs > out.txt; Get-Content out.txt | Select-Object -First 5

rules.name: shell-writes-code
rules.message: Writing code through PowerShell's text handling changes it on the way: Get-Content reads in the ANSI code page, and in a list the comma binds tighter than + (lesson 53). Use Edit or Write, or a node script written to a file.
